title: greenR — Urban Greenness Quantification Framework
description: Open-source R package and interactive Shiny web application for fine-scale quantification, spatial analysis, and visualization of street-level urban greenness and park accessibility using OpenStreetMap data. Awarded the Prix Carto 2025 by the Swiss Society of Cartography.
award: Prix Carto 2025 — Swiss Society of Cartography

title: Zürich Climate Solutions — Spatial Feasibility Assessment
description: Interactive 3D spatial decision-support platform for building-level climate adaptation in Zürich. Fuses eight open data layers across ~54,000 buildings to evaluate retrofit suitability (RSI), heat hazard intervention priorities, and adoption readiness.

title: Co-Creation Provenance Lab
description: An open-source platform tracing the provenance of citizen ideas and inputs in AI-moderated public consultations, ensuring transparency, voice preservation, and representational equity.

title: VAYU — Sensor Analytics & Statistical Processing Software
description: Open-source GUI software (Python/PyQt) for data processing, spatial-temporal visualization, and machine learning on crowd-sourced sensor data (AirBox, PurpleAir). Supports automated cleaning, Kalman imputation, and predictive modeling.

title: Trust-Based Dynamic Sensor Calibration
description: A dynamic consensus calibration mechanism for distributed low-cost PM2.5 sensor networks that eliminates the need for continuous physical co-location with reference monitors. Achieves up to 68% error reduction through multi-criteria trust modeling.

title: CAR: Clean Air Routing Algorithm
description: An algorithm and application framework that optimizes urban path navigation to minimize pedestrian PM2.5 exposure, integrating real-time sensor data with shortest-path algorithms.

title: Urban Green Equity Analysis
description: Moving beyond mean greenness metrics to reveal socio-spatial inequities in urban greenery distribution at the residential block level across Latin American cities.
